# getColumnPositionByLetter

<link-summary>Converts a column letter into its one-based position.</link-summary>

<web-summary>getColumnPositionByLetter() — Converts a column letter into its one-based position. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>appsscript/sheet</code> · Since: 1.0.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function getColumnPositionByLetter(letter: string): number | null;
```

Indices count from zero, the way a `GridRange` does; positions count from one, the way `getRange(row, column)` does. Mixing the two is the usual source of an off-by-one in a spreadsheet script, which is why both pairs exist under separate names.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type     | Description                        |
| :-------- | :------- | :--------------------------------- |
| `letter`  | `string` | The column letter, in either case. |

## Returns

`number | null` — the one-based position.

## Examples

### Converting

```javascript
getColumnPositionByLetter("A"); // => 1
getColumnPositionByLetter("AA"); // => 27
```
